report.summary: Analyzed run_gate docstring claims against code in chunk 4 of harness.py.

handoff.purpose: Define run_gate function with advisory regression ratchet logic.

symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Reads baseline.json, runs tier1, compares recall per task, returns dict with pass/fail and details.

claims.text: ADVISORY regression ratchet. Replays ``tasks`` (default TASKS) against a stored baseline.json and flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED.
claims.why: Code at line 869 iterates over result['per_task'], compares current recall to baseline recall for PRIMARY-tier tasks (line 889-890), and collects regressions when cur_recall < base_recall (line 894-898). Default tasks via all_tasks() at line 870.

claims.text: Compares PER TASK, never on a mean -- a mean hides one task collapsing while another improves
claims.why: Code loops over each task individually (line 876-903), comparing each task's recall to its own baseline. No averaging or aggregation of recall values.

claims.text: Workflow before shipping a slice-heuristic change: python -m daedalus.eval --gate
claims.why: CLI interface is not in this chunk; cannot verify that --gate invokes run_gate.

claims.text: Expect PASS. A FAIL means either a real regression (fix the slicer) or an intentional, reviewed label change -- in which case update the baseline EXPLICITLY (never automatically): python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline
claims.why: CLI behavior and update-baseline command are outside this chunk.

claims.text: GUARDRAIL: this gate is ADVISORY ONLY. It is a local developer command plus a unit test (there is no CI in this repo -- verified: no .github/workflows). It must never be wired to block an autonomous action.
claims.why: No evidence of CI or autonomous wiring in this chunk. The 'advisory' flag is set to True at line 907, but enforcement depends on caller.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (see ``run_tier1``) have no recall to compare and are SPLIT by tier, not folded into ``regressions``: * PRIMARY tier -- FAILS the gate loudly (``errored_primary``, named in the rendered report). * QUARANTINE tier -- reported only (``errored_quarantine``), never fails the gate.
claims.why: Code at line 879-884: if 'error' in t, classifies by _is_primary_tier into errored_primary or errored_quarantine. These are not added to regressions. At line 906, passed requires len(errored_primary)==0, so PRIMARY errors cause failure; QUARANTINE errors do not affect passed.

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- lane A1) are likewise SPLIT OUT, not folded into ``regressions``: a task that TRANSITIONS to focus-withheld this run has no ``recall`` to compare ... Reported in its own ``focus_withheld`` section, regardless of tier, and never fails the gate.
claims.why: Code at line 885-887: if t.get('focus_withheld'), appends to focus_withheld list and continues, skipping regression check. At line 906, passed only checks regressions and errored_primary; focus_withheld does not affect passed.

claims.text: tasks = all_tasks() if tasks is None else tasks
claims.why: Exact code at line 870: tasks = all_tasks() if tasks is None else tasks.

claims.why: Exact code at line 871: p = baseline_path or DEFAULT_BASELINE_PATH.

claims.why: Exact code at line 873: baseline_tasks = baseline.get("tasks", {}).

claims.why: Exact code at line 875: result = run_tier1(tasks).

observations.what: The docstring claims run_gate is 'ADVISORY ONLY' and 'must never be wired to block an autonomous action', but the code itself does not enforce this; it returns an 'advisory' flag but the caller could ignore it and block.
The docstring references 'rendered report' for errored_primary but the function only returns a dict; rendering is outside this chunk.
